action: Place probe to obtain an initial view. Verify orientation relative to the bony landmarks.
interpretation: Recognize the hyperechoic bone interface. Determine correct probe orientation on the screen.

action: Slide the probe distally (down). Center the view over the joint space.
interpretation: Utilize the joint space as the primary reference point for the scan.

action: Hold position over the joint space to define anatomical laterality.
interpretation: Identify the Femur located to the left of the screen and the Tibia located to the right.

action: Focus on the tissue spanning the joint space.
interpretation: Identify the Medial Collateral Ligament (MCL) as the "bright tissue" laying across the joint. Note that the ligament appears "super bright."

action: Inspect the space deep to the MCL.
interpretation: Visualize the "shadowing" or "shading" of the meniscus located directly underneath the MCL.

action: Scan the medial side of the knee specifically.
interpretation: Assess this location for intraarticular fluid, correlating with the clinical "brush test."

action: Trace the MCL structure distally along the tibia.
interpretation: Visualize the MCL as a "broad, flat band" of bright tissue overlying the tibia.

action: Scan the probe posteriorly along the MCL.
interpretation: Assess the posterior fibers of the ligament to cover the breadth of the band.

action: Scan the probe superiorly along the MCL.
interpretation: Inspect the fibers for any "break," "tearing," or a "loss of those tight striations" indicating pathology.

action: Position probe over the joint space for dynamic assessment. Instruct patient: 'Extend your knee slowly.'
interpretation: Look for a "little pocket of fluid" to push or bubble out from the joint space during movement.

action: Observe the fluid dynamics during the extension maneuver.
interpretation: Confirm intra-capsular pathology if fluid bubbles out. Distinguish this from interstitial swelling outside the capsule, which "will not move around at all."

action: Re-acquire the standard view of the medial compartment.
interpretation: Visualize the MCL, the joint space, and the medial meniscus.

action: Trace the anatomy distally, right to the edge of the tibial tuberosity.
interpretation: Follow the structure down onto the tibia.

action: Inspect the distinct structures overlying the tibia at this distal level.
interpretation: Identify "those tendons" appearing as "bright tissue" on top of the tibia.
